page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-192-lssd is an x86_64 server belonging to the Network Optimized family, designed for dense compute, high memory, and extensive local storage throughput. The system is provisioned with 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1488.0 GB of memory, resulting in a high memory density of 7.75 GB per core. It integrates 32 local NVMe SSDs providing an aggregated direct-attached capacity of 12885 GB. Hardware accelerators are absent, with the GPU count remaining at zero.

The inclusion of 12885 GB of local NVMe SSD storage paired with dedicated compute cores targets I/O-intensive data workloads. Compute resources operate without shared-core virtualization limits, ensuring stable processing across all 192 threads. Because the instance comes with high capacity local storage, operational throughput bypasses network-attached block storage constraints, though data durability requires application-level replication across instances due to the ephemeral nature of local SSDs.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the high resource density allows substantial workload consolidation. The pairing of extensive memory, substantial local storage arrays, and dedicated processing eliminates the operational cost of provisioning and attaching multiple external storage tiers. However, the machine size requires high, constant utilization to justify its large resource footprint.

This server type is primarily aligned with high-performance transactional databases, real-time in-memory data processing, distributed caching layers, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-intensive analytical operations requiring rapid local read/write cycles.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-192-lssd is a Network Optimized x86_64 cloud server featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs, 1488.0 GB of RAM, and 12885 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed over 32 disks. Delivering an allocation ratio of 7.75 GB of memory per core, this instance accommodates memory-demanding and data-dense systems without GPU acceleration. The massive local NVMe disk array facilitates ultra-low latency and elevated I/O throughput compared to network-attached alternatives, offsetting the need for decoupled disk volumes. The sheer resource profile targets enterprise-grade consolidation, offering cost-effective scale for environments capable of saturating 192 dedicated execution threads. Workloads matching this architecture include large distributed databases, in-memory processing frameworks, high-throughput caching, and extensive big data analytics requiring high storage bandwidth.
